scope: Paper-claim robustness supplement for the Phase-1 winner; this does not replace or modify the controller's preregistered three-seed gate.

known_at_registration: Seed-42 I0, I8, and I16 training and evaluation results.
I8 is the only mixed candidate that passes the seed-42 screen.
I32 seed-42 training is in progress and cannot enter candidate selection.
The fixed 30-problem train/evaluation lexical-overlap union and seed-42 sensitivity results.
unobserved_at_registration: All seed-43 training and evaluation results.
All seed-44 training and evaluation results.

selection_bias_rationale: Seed 42 selected I8 over I16, so a three-seed aggregate containing seed 42 is valid as the preregistered Phase-1 gate but is not by itself an unbiased held-out confirmation of stability.

claim_policy.stable_cross_seed_generalization: Allowed only if the preregistered three-seed primary gate, heldout_unfiltered_claim_gate, and heldout_overlap_filtered_claim_gate all pass.
claim_policy.phase1_pass_without_stable_claim: If the primary gate passes but either held-out claim gate fails, report a Phase-1 pass or promising initialization effect, but do not call the method stable across training seeds.
claim_policy.failure: If the preregistered primary gate fails, the method fails Phase 1 regardless of any held-out subset highlight.
claim_policy.i32_role: I32 remains a signal-only dose-response endpoint and cannot rescue or replace a failed mixed-candidate gate.

limitations: Only two held-out training seeds are available, so the held-out gate uses transparent point constraints rather than claiming a well-estimated training-seed population interval.
The 30-problem lexical exclusion is a fixed sensitivity set, not proof of semantic decontamination.
Passing these gates is necessary for the intended claim but does not replace comparisons against standard LoRA and other paper baselines.
